sūbŭlo , ōnis, m.
I. A flute-player, the Tuscan name for tibicen: “subulo Tusce tibicen dicitur. Itaque Ennius: Subulo quondam marinas propter astabat plagas,” Fest. p. 309 Müll.; cf. Varr. L. L. 7, § 35 ib. (Sat. v. 41 Vahl.).—
II. A kind of hart
with pointed horns, Plin. 11, 37, 45, § 213; 28, 17, 67, § 231. —
III. Perh. i. q. paedico, Aus. Epigr. 70.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
